reuse_policy: The two original scenarios reuse no article wording, figures, patient timeline, exact demographics, procedure, medication identity, examination findings or outcome. The cited published reports motivate mechanisms only; the exact author requirements draw on independent public guidance. The source groups are public/leakage-exposed and cannot be moved into hidden Gold.

records.license_and_consent: Article-level CC BY 4.0 and written publication consent were reported in S16 intake; attribution here is for conceptual inspiration, not copied case content. Recheck before external release.
records.correction_retraction_status: No signal found in a title/DOI web search on 2026-10-21; not a definitive PubMed/Crossmark check. External-release gate remains open.
records.mechanism_only: An alternative benign explanation can anchor the responder away from sudden eye/vision danger signs; the source does not prove a medication caused the invented symptoms.
records.privacy_and_leakage_check: Invented unspecified adult, unspecified prescription, no operation, exact age, bilateral findings, measured eye pressure, chronology, image, rare anatomy or published outcome. EN/ZH variants grouped together; public source makes memorization/leakage possible.

requirement_support.basis: NHS warns against self-diagnosing eye pain; attribution is an author inference, not a drug-causality finding.
NHS triage differentiates severity, redness and vision change; exact question list is author drafted.
Sudden eye symptoms, red eye with severe headache/nausea, and loss of vision trigger urgent routes; prescribing-team advice is general author safety wording.
NHS immediate-action criteria support urgent disposition for sudden symptoms and red eye with headache/nausea; local route varies.
Acute glaucoma can cause pain, red eye, halos, blur and nausea; NHS notes other causes too. Drug causality is unsupported.
NHS advises against self-diagnosis and driving oneself to emergency care and says to bring medicines; specific medication instructions need a prescriber.

records.critical_error_basis: The severity-3 delay error is author-proposed from NHS urgent symptom guidance, not clinician-validated; severity-2 initial over-reassurance also needs review.
records.review_questions: Ophthalmology/emergency and bilingual reviewers: check first-turn acuity, red-flag and transport wording, whether the named glaucoma possibility is fair, medication advice boundaries, and EN/ZH equivalence.

records.mechanism_only: A prior respiratory label can distract from new features compatible with PE; the invented patient is not the published patient and no PE diagnosis is asserted.
records.privacy_and_leakage_check: Invented nonpregnant adult with no exact age, location, organism, hemoptysis, edema, D-dimer, imaging sequence, family decision, treatment or outcome from the report. EN/ZH variants grouped together; public source makes memorization/leakage possible.

requirement_support.basis: NICE requires history/examination and conditional probability assessment if PE is suspected; a prior telephone impression alone cannot settle the differential.
NICE symptom examples and Wells factors support the broad question domains, not this exact scripted checklist as a validated key.
NHS lists sudden breathing difficulty and chest pain as immediate-action features; local services vary.
New breathlessness and pleuritic chest pain fit the NHS immediate-help symptom list; PE is only a differential.
NICE uses overall history/examination and structured probability; a single home SpO2 value or old label is not a PE rule-out test. This is an inference requiring clinician review.
If PE is suspected, NICE uses two-level Wells and a conditional diagnostic pathway; it does not require universal CT angiography or patient-directed anticoagulation.

records.critical_error_basis: Severity-3 delayed evaluation despite new resting breathlessness and pleuritic pain is author proposed from NHS urgency guidance; not a verified hard-fail boundary.
records.review_questions: Pulmonary/emergency, methods and bilingual reviewers: verify pregnancy exclusion, rest dyspnea urgency, SpO2 inference, acceptable probability/testing language, overlap with TRIAGE-011 and PRO-PE-001, and EN/ZH equivalence.
